summary.intent: Continue executing the checker-first plan for the caliper/tsrs project: resolve the tuple-normalization review finding on slice 1 (PR #391), keep remaining slices moving with agents, and clarify why no open trails were visible.
summary.outcome: Tuple normalization was fixed via a single `normalize_tuple` function, verified with goldens and a full gate, and PR #391 merged into main. A parity-check worker was started alongside slice 2, and trail #255 was closed. Branch and worktree cleanup was denied by the classifier and left undone.

repo: `PropType::Tuple` is built only in `tuple_of`, so tuple normalization is enforced in one place: `normalize_tuple` in `crates/core/src/resolver/collected.rs`. `tuple_of` serves both type resolution and signature types.

Tuple normalization rules follow the Go checker: an optional before the last required becomes required plus `undefined`; first rest through last optional/rest collapses to one rest of the union; a single-rest tuple becomes the array type; `readonly` wraps the finished tuple. A generic variadic inside the collapse range is a documented limitation.

Cache schema version and output schema version only need a bump when stored or wire shapes change. A change to resolved values alone does not need one. After the slice 1 merge, cache is 33 and output schema is 5.
The construct suite fixtures (`tuples-arrays/33` to `40`) carry Go checker goldens. A clean-room oracle test catches new fixtures that were never `git add`ed.
The gate is `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just semver`, clean-room nextest, and `construct:check` plus oracle tests.
ADR 0026 requires a tsrs-versus-Go parity check on every tsrs version bump, run via `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity`.
Stacked branches use signed merge commits only, never rebase. GitHub deletes the base branch when its PR merges, so dependent branches must merge `origin/main` and link with `--base main`.
Slices 2 to 6 all edit `crates/semantic` and the pipeline, so they must run serially. Only the parity check is disjoint.

code.finding: `tuple_of` is called here for type resolution. It is the sole builder of `PropType::Tuple` and the enforcement point for `normalize_tuple`.
Signature types also go through `tuple_of`, so tuple normalization applies to function signatures too.

workflow: Subagent reports are model output and not user approval. Verify claims such as MERGEABLE state and CI status before relying on them.
Use Workflow fan-out only when outputs are disjoint, as with the construct suite. Serial dependent slices gain nothing from extra agents and risk conflicts.
A subagent that cannot read the upstream source reconstructs rules from memory. Validate them empirically against goldens and disclose the caveat in the PR body.
Prove a new test with a pre-fix revert: the test fails without the fix and passes with it.
Trails with no open changes drop out of an open-changes view even while the trail stays open.
Do not remove worktrees before their PRs merge.

friction: The classifier denied deleting the merged remote branch `feat/construct-suite` and removing clean, pushed worktrees as destructive git actions.
The slice 2 worker was told to merge `origin/feat/proptype-variants`, which GitHub had deleted on merge. A correction message was needed to avoid a failed merge or a PR stacked on a deleted base.
The user saw no open trails because the open changes had merged. This needed investigation and an explanation.
The tuple worker could not read the typescript-go source and had no fetch access, so the rules came from memory.
The tuple worker initially forgot to `git add` the new fixtures. The clean-room oracle test caught it.
CI on #391 was still pending (17 checks) at hand-back, so results were unknown.
open_items: Accept ADR 0026, which blocks slice 4 and the default flip.
Decide on release PR #291, which covers 61 changes.
Decide whether `@tsrs/<platform>` becomes an npm dependency, which adds 23 to 50 MB per platform per install.
Slice 2 (`feat/checker-converter`) and `test/tsrs-parity` (trail #259) are still in progress. The parity check has no CI job yet.
Slice 3 (React terminals by declaring path), watch mode (S6), the generic instantiation probe (S5), and the default flip (S4/S8) wait on slice 2 and ADR 0026.
The `SPEC/AC` tag re-scan is deferred because it touches files slice 7 will delete.
The remote branch `feat/construct-suite` still needs deleting by the user, and `chore/changesets-for-merged-fixes` and `perf/cycles-by-structure` await a decision.
40 local worktrees are left in place.
Limitation: a generic variadic inside a tuple collapse range is not normalized, because `PropType` has no `T[number]` shape.
